name: TensorFlow
summary: An end-to-end machine-learning platform with tensor operations, eager and graph-oriented execution paths, explicit device/runtime placement, and a SavedModel serialization boundary.

features.name: Eager operation runtime
features.description: EagerContext owns tensor handles, devices, function libraries, executors, rendezvous, and distributed execution context; EagerExecute can run locally, asynchronously, or on a remote task.
benefits: Supports immediate tensor experimentation and runtime control flow
Uses one context to coordinate local, asynchronous, and remote execution
costs: Execution timing and synchronization differ between synchronous and asynchronous paths
Remote execution introduces transport and rendezvous failure boundaries

features.name: Explicit and soft device placement runtime
features.description: The eager context tracks devices and selects a suitable device for an operation from a preferred device description, with optional soft placement when an exact match is unavailable.
benefits: Makes heterogeneous CPU, accelerator, and remote device execution available through one operation model
Can fall back to a suitable device when configured to allow soft placement
costs: Placement affects transfers, performance, and numerical/runtime behavior
Unavailable or incorrectly configured devices turn placement into an execution failure

features.name: Serialized SavedModel MetaGraph boundary
features.description: SavedModel is a versioned high-level serialization format containing one or more MetaGraphDef records, providing a persistence boundary for TensorFlow models and signatures.
benefits: Separates model exchange and serving artifacts from an in-process runtime
Allows a SavedModel to carry multiple MetaGraphs under one schema
costs: Compatibility depends on schema versions, signatures, assets, variables, and runtime support
Serialization captures a model boundary rather than arbitrary live runtime state

features.name: Function-library and distributed rendezvous substrate
features.description: The eager context integrates a process function library runtime, rendezvous manager, distributed worker environment, and collective executor manager for functions and cross-task coordination.
benefits: Shares operation and function execution abstractions across local and distributed contexts
Provides runtime hooks for coordination and collective execution
costs: Distributed coordination adds lifecycle, ordering, and failure complexity
Correctness depends on matching worker, rendezvous, and collective configuration

mathematical_views.model: Operation dataflow graph with eager execution semantics
mathematical_views.question: How can tensor operations be understood as a dataflow graph while preserving immediate, asynchronous, and remote execution choices?
assumptions: Tensor handles are graph values and operations are graph nodes
Execution mode and device placement are explicit runtime state
Remote and asynchronous execution preserve operation input/output contracts but not identical timing

mathematical_views.question: Given an operation's preferred device and the devices in a context, when does placement select an exact device, a soft fallback, or failure?
assumptions: The preferred device is a constraint over device attributes
The context's device set and soft-placement policy are fixed during one decision
Transfer cost is analyzed separately from placement feasibility

mathematical_views.question: Which live model structures can be refined into a SavedModel containing one or more MetaGraphs while remaining loadable by a compatible runtime?
assumptions: SavedModel schema version and MetaGraphDef contracts are explicit
Signatures, variables, assets, and function bodies are included in the persistence boundary as required
Loadability and numerical equivalence are separate validation questions

benefits: Immediate execution with local, asynchronous, and remote options
costs: Multiple execution modes complicate timing and failure reasoning

benefits: One operation model spans heterogeneous devices
costs: Placement and transfer choices affect performance and availability

benefits: Portable model artifact and serving boundary
costs: Schema and runtime compatibility constrain portability

benefits: Reusable function and coordination substrate across tasks
costs: Coordination state and distributed failure handling add operational complexity
